## Methodology and caveats

- **Frozen synthetic world.** The models and offline suites use fixture places (synthetic attributes on real or OSM-derived names), fixed weather, events, travel and a frozen clock (Thursday 2026-11-05 10:00 IST, target Saturday 2026-11-07). Every model sees identical tool results, so rows are comparable, but scores describe this small world, not live data quality.
- **Independent checks.** Hard assertions recompute cost, time, opening hours, evidence, pacing, daylight, Plan B, prose and grounding from the raw fixture files and from the request text, never from the planner's own validation flags. Every stop must have been returned by a provider during the same run (recorded by proxies around the providers). Case-specific assertions are code where machine-checkable; a few use keyword proxies for "the text mentions X" (marked in their detail). Assertions that need a browser or judgement are marked `judge` and never count toward the hard pass rate.
- **Hard pass** requires every applicable code assertion, including the status being in the case's expected set: a deterministic fallback on a feasible case is a failure for a model row.
- **Clarification precision/recall** count one instance per planner call; the first call of a case that supplies `clarification_answers` counts as blocking (the spec provides answers because a question is expected), its resume call as non-blocking.
- **Separation.** Baseline (no LLM), hosted API and local (Ollama) rows are separate populations. Local rows get a 240 s run deadline instead of 60 s; their latency is reported, not hidden. Holdout cases are reported separately and must never be tuned against.
- **Sample size.** n is shown for every number. With one repeat per case, a single flaky run moves a rate by several points; use three repeats (pass^3) before drawing conclusions.
- **Judge.** No judge model ran, so judge quality is null (shown as —).
